story_type: shark bite far offshore, swimmer and litter hoist from a ship plowing through whitecaps (hoist cam)
hook: A shark bit his hand 100 miles out to sea.
narration: A shark bit this man's hand a hundred miles out to sea.
He was fifty-eight, aboard a ship about one hundred miles west of San Diego.
A Coast Guard helicopter crew from San Diego lowered a rescue swimmer to the deck.
The ship kept moving the whole time. A steady course gives the pilot a predictable target to hover over.
Next, the litter came down, swinging over the whitecaps.
The crew strapped him in for the ride up.
[short pause] Then the swimmer rode the cable back up last.
outcome: And the helicopter crew flew the man to a local hospital.

location_card.place: 100 miles west of San Diego, California

title: Shark bite 100 miles off San Diego
description:
On Aug. 10, 2015, a Coast Guard Sector San Diego MH-60 helicopter crew medically evacuated a 58-year-old man with a shark bite to his right hand from a ship about 100 miles west of San Diego, and flew him to a local hospital.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video by Sector San Diego, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/419352/coast-guard-medevacs-man-100-miles-west-san-diego
